hypothesis: A candidate must not be able to change the trusted corpus collector, response validator, or workflow executable path used to authorize that same candidate.

falsification_cases.mutation: candidate replaces platform_candidate_review.py corpus builder with code that omits a blocking file
falsification_cases.required_result: trusted collector output remains unchanged and includes the blocking file

falsification_cases.mutation: candidate replaces validation logic with unconditional valid/PASS
falsification_cases.required_result: trusted validator still rejects a structurally invalid or contradictory PASS

falsification_cases.mutation: candidate adds a same-named trust-kernel module earlier on candidate PYTHONPATH
falsification_cases.required_result: trusted executable provenance remains bound to frozen trust-kernel identity and candidate module is never imported

falsification_cases.mutation: candidate modifies the candidate-side review workflow to point execution back to candidate code
falsification_cases.required_result: candidate-side workflow has no promotion authority; only separately invoked frozen trust-kernel workflow evidence can count

pass_criteria: trusted collector and validator bytes are identified by an immutable commit/hash independent of candidate commit
candidate checkout is treated as untrusted evidence only
candidate code is not on the trusted kernel import path
candidate-side review execution has authority NONE even if it returns PASS
kernel cannot approve a change to its own trusted bytes without a separately governed kernel-upgrade process
all L7 mutation cases pass deterministically without any LLM/provider API call
failure_rule: Any candidate-controlled path capable of changing trusted collection, validation, or promotion authority is a mechanism defect and keeps EXP-L nonpromotable.
